findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer guarantees fresh data — silent behavior change for existing callers
findings.rationale: The old `GET /pulls/:id` attempted a live GitHub fetch and, on success, returned fresh data. The new implementation always returns whatever is in the database without any network call. Any deployed caller (e.g., e2e tests, CI runner, external consumer) that relies on this endpoint returning up-to-date PR details will now silently receive stale data. The response shape is unchanged, but the semantic contract of freshness is broken. The PR description acknowledges this trade-off but provides no migration path or deprecation for existing callers.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer backfills diff stats — fields may be null/0 for PRs from list
findings.rationale: The old GET route updated `additions`, `deletions`, and `filesCount` on the pull request record from the GitHub detail. The new GET route does not perform this update. PRs that were imported from a list (which lacks these stats) will return `null` or `0` for these fields until `POST /pulls/:id/refresh` is called. Callers that depend on these fields being populated after a GET (e.g., the PR list page) will see incomplete data.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer populates files/commits/stats from GitHub
findings.rationale: Previously the GET handler fetched the latest files, commits, and diff stats from GitHub and persisted them before returning. Now it returns only whatever is already stored in the database. A caller that does not call POST /pulls/:id/refresh first will see empty files/commits and possibly null/zero stats for a PR that has never been refreshed. This is a behavioral change: the GET no longer guarantees that the returned data is fresh or even populated. External consumers that relied on the implicit refresh side effect will silently get stale or empty data.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response no longer includes extra fields from GitHub API
findings.rationale: The old handler spread the GitHub API response (`...detail`) into the return object, which could include undocumented fields (e.g., `mergeable`, `rebaseable`, `labels`). The new handler constructs a fixed object with only the fields listed in the PrDetail type. Any caller that relied on those extra fields (even accidentally) will now get `undefined` for them. This narrows the contract.

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response shape narrowed – extra GitHub fields removed

Any caller that reads `response.user`, `response.labels`, or other GitHub-specific fields will now get `undefined` silently. This breaks the contract for all consumers that depend on the full GitHub payload.
